title: Migration header comment contradicts the shipped token-lifecycle and erasure design (stale capability-model documentation)
evidence:
Migration header: "* Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row." and "-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request)." — contradicted within the same file by the erased_at column comment ("keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close") and by the in-chunk spec change log: "W1: tokens mint at SAVE time (upsert arg 4, COALESCE keeps existing)" and "W3: erasure is a tombstone (fields/token wiped, erased_at set, email kept as suppression record until vacancy close)" (_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-form-save-resume-f3.md).
detail: The schema's own documentation of a capability-token auth model misstates when tokens are minted (save-time, not first link request, so most rows are NOT NULL-token) and what erasure does (tombstone, not row delete). Future security/compliance audits reading the migration will reason from a wrong threat model.
recommended_fix: Update the header comment to state tokens mint at save time (COALESCE-preserved) and erasure writes an erased_at tombstone retaining (vacancy_id, email) as a suppression record until vacancy close.
